title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes, Grothendieck works with 'ateliers' (also called 'atlas'). An atelier is a structure (M, ≤, ≪, 𝔉): M is a poset of (multi)localities, 𝔉 is a set of 'figures', and At 1–At 8 are its axioms. Model examples are Pf(M) and Fig(L). Fig(L) is roughly the nonempty (finite) subsets, or 'figures', of a set L of points, ordered by inclusion. The previous page started a list of examples of morphisms of ateliers. Example 1 there: a map of sets f: L → L' induces f*: Fig(L') → Fig(L) by pulling back and discarding empty preimages.

This page:

(2) The canonical map 𝔉 → Fig(M) is an injective morphism of ateliers satisfying the 'bijectivity condition' (1.54). Roughly, (1.54) says the map on sub-figures below a given figure is bijective. Composing with Fig(M) → Fig(L), induced (contravariantly, as in Example 1) by a map L → M, gives a morphism 𝔉 → Fig(L). This composite still satisfies (1.54) but need not be injective. Axiom At 8 is apparently what is at stake for non-injectivity.

Definition (plongement / embedding). A morphism f: 𝔉' → 𝔉 is an embedding if:
- (a) f(𝔉') is a sub-atelier of 𝔉;
- (b) f induces an isomorphism 𝔉' ≅ f(𝔉').

Explicitly, writing F = f(F'):
- (a') for every F' the map Sousfig(F') → Sousfig(F), G' ↦ f(G'), is bijective. Injectivity is noted to come for free when f is injective. Surjectivity means every G ≤ F is f(G') for some G' ≤ F'. So the image is downward closed (a sieve).
- (b') f reflects the order: f(G') ≤ f(F') ⇒ G' ≤ F'.

In modern terms, f is an order-isomorphism onto a down-closed sub-poset, compatible with the extra structure. The next page proves sufficiency: surjectivity on sub-figures plus injectivity of f gives order-reflection.

The page sets up the next definition. An atlas is 'ensembliste' if the canonical 𝔉 → Fig(L) is an embedding. Equivalently (At ens 1): multloc(F) ≪ multloc(G) ⇒ F ≪ G, i.e. a figure is determined, order-theoretically, by its underlying set of points. This is the analogue of the difference between an abstract simplicial complex (simplices determined by vertex sets) and a Δ-complex / semi-simplicial or regular-cell structure.

Purpose: to isolate, within the combinatorial models of tame ('modérée') spaces, those that are 'set-like', like simplicial complexes.
errors: Labelling of the equivalent conditions is muddled. On p.52 the proof says 'Par b'), … ∃ Ḡ' ≤ F' with f(Ḡ') = f(G')', which is really the surjectivity part of a'). It then uses 'a)' (injectivity) to conclude G' = Ḡ'. The roles of a'/b' appear swapped or overwritten in the draft.

The cancelled 'a) f est injectif' and the marginal NB ('Si f est injective, alors a) ⇒ a')') show the definition was being reworked in real time. The final equivalence is stated only partially (the necessity direction is merely called 'évidemment nécessaire'). There is no mathematical error, just incomplete drafting.

ideas.what: Canonical morphism 𝔉 → Fig(M) and its composite with Fig(M) → Fig(L) induced by a map L → M; the composite keeps the sub-figure bijectivity condition but loses injectivity
ideas.modern_name: realization / vertex-scheme map of a cell-like poset into the full simplex on its points
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard combinatorial topology (abstract simplicial complexes, face posets)

ideas.what: Embedding of ateliers = morphism whose image is a sub-atelier (down-closed) and which is an isomorphism onto its image; equivalently bijective on sub-figure sets plus order-reflecting
ideas.modern_name: sieve inclusion / order-embedding onto a lower set (full subcomplex-type inclusion)

ideas.what: 'Ensembliste' atlas: the canonical map to Fig(L) is an embedding, i.e. figures are determined by their underlying point sets (At ens 1)
ideas.modern_name: abstract simplicial complex condition vs. Δ-complex / regular CW (cells determined by vertex sets)
ideas.where_published: Framework of tame topology announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but the 'atelier' formalism is unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: The 'atelier' axiomatics for tame topology is itself unpublished and of some historical interest. However, this page only contains routine definitions (embeddings as isomorphisms onto down-closed sub-structures, and a simplicial-complex-type 'set-like' condition) with no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'Fil(L)' should read 'Fig(L)' (the morphism Fig(M) → Fig(L) of Example 1).
'At δ' is almost certainly 'At 8' (axiom 8 of the atelier axioms At 1–At 8 mentioned on p.52).
'induit par [?] un [?] de L → M' should be read as induced by an application L → M (contravariant pullback as in Example 1 on p.50).
Left margin likely reads 'Convention … voir page 47' (referring to the definition of morphism of ateliers p.47, also referenced by '(1.47) ✓').
